approach: Root cause: the guard reads real `df` and the shared test config leaves the minimum at the 10 GB default. Fix both ends. (1) test_config gets `[disk] min_free_gb = 0` so every CLI test, including the nested run, ignores real free space. (2) disk.rs `df_free_bytes` gains an env override `ATHENA_FREE_BYTES` (read only when set and numeric) so a spawned binary can be shown a simulated low reading; production default 10 GB untouched. A new binary test runs the nested ask/go with 9 GB simulated and passes because the config minimum is 0; a negative control with minimum 10 fails with 'environment: low disk', proving the injection is effective. Drain tests that assert the 10 GB hold rely on the default today; they switch to a fixture with min_free_gb = 10 set explicitly via a new helper. disk.rs gets unit tests for the override. CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Set `[disk] min_free_gb = 0` in test_config (appended after the base config) with a comment, and add helper `with_min_free_gb(config, gb)` in common/mod.rs that rewrites that line.
decisions.reason: Fixes the shared fixture, not one test; drain tests that need the guard can set 10 explicitly.

rejected.option: Set 0 only in the nested-run test
rejected.why: Leaves every other binary test dependent on real disk.

rejected.option: Change the production default or athena.toml
rejected.why: Out of scope and would weaken the guard.

decisions.choice: Inject the reading by env var ATHENA_FREE_BYTES inside df_free_bytes, honored only when set to a valid integer.
decisions.reason: The nested run is a spawned binary, so a fn-pointer injection (with_free_space) cannot reach it; env crosses the process boundary and the guard code path stays the same.

rejected.why: Does not show the nested run is exercised under low free space.
Larger change to production command surface.

decisions.choice: Keep in-process drain tests on with_free_space/simulated_free and give them min_free_gb = 10 explicitly.
decisions.reason: They already simulate values and never read real df; only the minimum needs pinning now that the fixture default is 0.

rejected.why: With the fixture minimum at 0 the 3 GB simulated readings no longer hold or fail, so the hold and fail-fast tests would break.

files.purpose: df_free_bytes honors ATHENA_FREE_BYTES when set and numeric; module docs; unit tests on a pure parse helper (no process-env mutation).
test_config appends [disk] min_free_gb = 0 with explanatory comment; add with_min_free_gb helper.
Add the companion nested-run test with simulated 9 GB and the min-10 negative control.
Disk hold/fail-fast tests build their Fixture with min_free_gb = 10 explicitly.

steps: disk.rs: add const FREE_BYTES_ENV = "ATHENA_FREE_BYTES", a pure helper turning an optional string into Option<u64>, use it at the top of df_free_bytes; update module docs; add unit tests.
common/mod.rs: append a comment plus `[disk]` and `min_free_gb = 0` to test_config's output; add pub fn with_min_free_gb.
drain.rs: switch the disk tests (go_with_disk callers and the_real_steps_hold test) to a fixture with min_free_gb = 10.
binary.rs: factor the nested ask/go into a helper taking an optional env var; add the companion test (9 GB simulated, passes) and the negative control (min 10, fails with low disk).
Run cargo fmt, clippy, and the full cargo test.

risks.risk: An env override in production code could mask real low disk if set by accident.
risks.mitigation: Document as a test hook, honored only if set and a valid integer; invalid values fall through to df.

risks.risk: Env mutation in core unit tests races with parallel tests.
risks.mitigation: Unit-test a pure helper taking the optional string; binary tests set env on the child Command only.

risks.risk: Drain tests asserting 10 GB break once the fixture default is 0.
risks.mitigation: Run the full drain test file; add the min-10 fixture to each affected test and check required amounts remain 10.0 GB.

risks.risk: Appended [disk] conflicts if base config later gains a [disk] table.
risks.mitigation: Use with_min_free_gb(&test_config(), 10) which rewrites the line, not a second table.

demonstrations.method: Run the binary test file. a_nested_run_works_in_a_scratch_copy_with_fake_agents passes; the new companion test runs the same nested ask/go with ATHENA_FREE_BYTES=9000000000 and passes; a control with min_free_gb = 10 and the same env fails with the low-disk text.
demonstrations.observes: All tests in binary pass; the companion shows exit 0 and the landing commit under 9 GB simulated; the control run exits non-zero mentioning 'environment: low disk: 9.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required'.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without min_free_gb = 0 in test_config the companion test fails with 'environment: low disk: 9.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required'; without the ATHENA_FREE_BYTES override the simulation has no effect and the negative-control assertion (min 10 must fail with low disk) fails.

demonstrations.method: Run core disk unit tests (including the new override tests); also run the drain tests that assert hold and fail-fast with simulated 3 GB: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain low_disk, and cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain the_real_steps_hold.
demonstrations.observes: Core disk tests pass; the drain hold test shows the job Proposed with 'environment: low disk: 3.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required'; the before-checks test shows a Failed job with a retry hint.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the guard stopped comparing against the minimum, the hold test (queued, 3.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required) and the fail-fast test would fail; the new disk.rs unit tests fail if the override is ignored or garbage is not ignored.

demonstrations.method: Read common/mod.rs test_config for the [disk] min_free_gb = 0 block and its comment; run the athena-data config tests, which still assert min_free_gb() == 10 for an absent [disk] table; git diff shows no change to athena-data.
demonstrations.observes: Config tests pass with default 10; the diff touches only the listed files.

demonstrations.method: Run cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt --all --check. CLI tests use min 0 or simulated readings.
demonstrations.fails_without: A test that still read real df with a nonzero minimum would flip with machine space; none remain (the_real_reader test only asserts > 0).

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff: an entry under [Unreleased] stating tests no longer depend on real free disk, that test_config sets [disk] min_free_gb = 0, and that ATHENA_FREE_BYTES simulates the reading.
demonstrations.observes: The new bullet is present in the Unreleased section.
